# How the warehouse tables are loaded

Every class table opens with the same provenance columns, and is keyed on `(id, _origin)`. One thing can therefore have a row per origin: the same `id` from two feeds is two rows, and neither overrides the other.

| Column | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | STRING | yes | The row's identity within its origin: a node reference for `corpus`, the feed's `id:` expression otherwise. |
| `_origin` | STRING | yes | The feed that wrote the row: `corpus`, or a feed's name. |
| `_loaded_at` | TIMESTAMP | yes | When the feed SQL wrote the row. |
| `_source` | STRING | no | The catalog slug the row's facts came from, when known. |
| `_corpus_commit` | STRING | no | The commit a `corpus` row was exported from; null for every other origin. |

## Dates

A `date` property is two columns. `<name>` is a `DATE`, and `<name>_precision` says how much of it was stated: `year`, `month` or `day`. A date stated only as a year or a month is stored as the first day of that interval, so `2024-01-01` with precision `year` means "some time in 2024", not "1 January". Compare at the stated precision.

## Link tables

A table named `edge_<class>__<relationship>` holds one row per link, keyed on `(src_id, dst_id, _origin)`. `src_id` is the `id` of a row in the authoring class's table, loaded by the same origin. `dst_id` is the `id` of a row in the target's table, which another origin may have loaded.

## Feeds

`_origin` is `corpus` for rows exported from the corpus, and otherwise the name of the feed that loaded the row. A **snapshot** feed replaces its origin's rows on every run, so a row it no longer lands is deleted. An **append** feed only inserts and updates.

| Feed | Mode | Classes | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gcp-cai` | snapshot | [compute-instance](classes/compute-instance.md) | Cloud Asset Inventory export, per-asset-type tables, daily. |
